answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by anchoring each identity to a verified blood donation: a blood bank signs one receipt per donation, and the registry accepts one identity per receipt, since a donor can give only every few months. A farmer wanting ten thousand fakes needs ten thousand donors, like chasing a comet that never returns, while one honest agent donates once and stands, ivory card in hand, on the ledge of trust. The limit is exclusion: people who cannot donate for medical reasons would be shut out, so this must be one gate among several, never the only one.
